title: From Single-Agent Self-Discovery to Multi-Agent Adaptation: Scaling Laws of Partner Feedback and Convention Rigidity in Meta Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
summary: Across more than 1,800 runs in simulated collective-robotics and coordination tasks, partner swaps revealed that apparent team-return gains could conceal lower focal-agent performance. Results also showed sensitivity to reciprocal partner feedback; they are simulation findings.
ai_technology: Disco103 and OPEN meta-learned reinforcement-learning update rules
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Across 1,800+ simulated runs, four-cell partner swaps found an apparent +1.066 team-return gain alongside a −0.119 focal-agent loss in a reported setting.
evidence.unknown: The results concern specified VMAS and Overcooked simulations; they do not establish performance in physical multi-agent systems.
evidence.ai_role: Disco103 and OPEN meta-learned reinforcement-learning update rules

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
